_readme: All lengths in mm. Keys starting with '_' are notes and are ignored. Run: python generate.py [other_params.json]

rail._note: MIL-STD-1913 Picatinny profile. Only change these if your rail measures differently.
rail._RAIL_WIDTH: Across the rail at its widest point, the outward point on each side
rail._RAIL_NECK_WIDTH: Width of the rail's top face, and of the neck where it meets the rifle. The sides run out from the top face to RAIL_WIDTH and back in to the neck at 45 degrees

clamp._note: Two-piece clamp: the fixed jaw is part of the body, the moving jaw is a separate part pulled in by bolts that run across under the rail into nuts slid into traps in the fixed side. Printed recoil lugs on the clamp floor sit in the rail's cross slots.
clamp._CLAMP_LENGTH: Length of the rail clamp along the rail (X). The body under it is longer; its length comes from the linkage
clamp._CLAMP_WALL: Side wall outside the rail top width
clamp._CLAMP_FLOOR: Base plate top to rail top. The clamp bolts and nut traps run through here, under the rail
clamp._JAW_LIP: How far the jaw lips hook up under the rail's widest point, towards the rifle. Must stay short of the neck ((RAIL_WIDTH - RAIL_NECK_WIDTH) / 2 = 2.8)
clamp._RAIL_CLEARANCE: Gap on each flank between rail and jaw
clamp._FLOOR_GAP: Gap under the rail top so the clamp pulls on the flanks, not the top
clamp._JAW_SPLIT_Y: Where the moving jaw is split off from the body (Y from rail centre line)
clamp._JAW_GAP: Clamping travel between moving jaw and body
clamp._BOLT_SPACING: Clamp bolt centre to centre along the rail; keep the nut traps clear of the recoil lugs
clamp._LUG_SPACING_SLOTS: Recoil lug spacing in rail slot pitches (1 = 10.01 mm)
clamp._LUG_HEIGHT: How far the lugs reach into the rail slots (slots are RAIL_SLOT_DEPTH deep)
clamp._LUG_WIDTH: Along the rail; the slots are RAIL_SLOT_WIDTH wide
clamp._BASE_PLATE: Plate the moving jaw rests on; also the roof of the screw channel

body._note: Open-bottomed channel under the clamp that holds the lead screw, slider and links.
body._END_WALL: End walls carry the screw: the knob pushes on one, the screw tip sits in the other
body._BOTTOM_WALL: Material under the leg pin hole and under the slider pin slots, along the bottom edge of the side walls. The leg's load comes in here
body._SIDE_CLEARANCE: Gap on each side between parts that slide or swing past each other

screw._note: Printed lead screw along the rail, 45 degree flanks so it prints upright without supports. Self-locking, so the leg stays put.
screw._SCREW_THREAD_CLEARANCE: Added to the slider's internal thread, radially and axially. Raise if the slider binds
screw._SCREW_HOLE_CLEARANCE: Radial gap for the screw journal and tip in the end walls
screw._CLIP_SNAP: How much narrower the retaining clip's slot is than the groove it snaps over. Raise if the clip falls off, lower if it will not go on

linkage._note: Leg pivots at the knob end of the body; twin links run from the slider pin down to the leg. Run the generator to see the height range and how far one knob turn moves the foot.
linkage._LEG_LENGTH: Leg pin to foot pin. Longer = more height range
linkage._LINK_PIVOT: Leg pin to link pin, along the leg
linkage._LEG_ANGLE_MIN: Leg angle below horizontal when fully retracted (slider against the far end wall)
linkage._LEG_ANGLE_MAX: Leg angle when fully extended (slider runs off the thread onto the screw journal)
linkage._LEG_WIDTH: Leg thickness across the rifle; also the slider tongue the links straddle
linkage._LEG_HUB_RADIUS: Round ends of the leg around the leg and foot pins

hardware._note: Every joint uses the same bolt: socket head, washer under the head, plain hex nut. The run checks each joint reaches through its nut.
hardware._BUSHING_DIAMETER: Printed tube the slider, link and foot pins turn on; the bolt clamps it solid so the plain nut can be tightened
hardware._BUSHING_CLEARANCE: Radial gap between the bushing and the hole it turns in

sled._note: Sled foot runs along the rail so the rifle slides straight back under recoil, and pivots on the end of the leg so it stays flat at any height. Both ends curl up like sledge runners; the curve starts at 45 degrees so it prints without supports.
sled._SLED_TIP_HEIGHT: Top of the curled tips above the running surface
sled._SLED_CURVE_RADIUS: Radius of the runner curve at each end
sled._SLED_TIP_FILLET: Concave curve where the tips rise out of the deck
sled._FOOT_PIVOT_HEIGHT: Foot pin above the deck top
sled._CHEEK_THICKNESS: Cheeks either side of the leg end

knob._note: Printed in one piece with the lead screw, on the knob end of the body. Engraved UP with a clockwise arrow.
knob._KNOB_GAP: Gap between the knob and the end wall in the preview

output._note: Point these somewhere else in a copy of this file to keep several variants side by side.
output._PREVIEW_RAIL: Draw a ghost Picatinny rail in the preview to check the fit
output._CHECK_CLEARANCES: Check the moving parts for overlaps at both ends and the middle of the travel (slower)
